reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 3x3 grid of 3x3 blocks; a block holds a copy of the input where the input cell at that block position is non-background, else it is empty.
why: block (i,j) of the output equals the input iff input(i,j) is fg, otherwise all background
invariants: the copied unit is the unchanged input

reading: The 6-row input is a vertically periodic pattern; it is continued with its smallest period to 9 rows and colour 1 is recoloured to 2.

slots.period: smallest vertical period of the input rows (2, 4 or 3 in training)

why: output row r equals input row (r mod period) with 1 replaced by 2

reading: The objects sitting on the bottom row are taken left to right and chained diagonally from the top-left corner: the first object's top-left goes to (0,0), and each next object's top-left goes on the previous object's bottom-right cell, overwriting it.

slots.subjects: the objects, ordered left to right
slots.link: next object's top-left cell = previous object's bottom-right cell

why: each object keeps shape and colour; consecutive objects share exactly one corner cell

reading: A 3x3 shape has small marker pieces of other colours next to it on some sides (including diagonals); in each marker's direction the shape is repeated in the marker's colour every 4 cells until the border.

slots.directions: the side/diagonal where each marker piece lies relative to the shape

why: every copy is the shape's exact mask recoloured, at offsets k*4 along the marker direction, k>=1

reading: Identical rectangular tiles repeat on a regular grid but are corrupted by noise, and noise is scattered outside; each tile is replaced by the cell-wise majority of all tiles and everything outside the tiles is cleared.

slots.tiles: the repeated equal-size rectangles (rows/cols bands where the pattern occurs)
slots.consensus: per-cell majority colour over all tiles

why: every tile in the output is the same majority pattern; all non-tile cells are background

reading: Like a self-tile: the 3x3 input becomes a 3x3 grid of blocks, and each block at a non-background input position holds the colour-inverted input (fg cells become background, background cells take the colour); other blocks are empty.

slots.extent: fg cells of the input pick the blocks
slots.unit: input with background and its single colour swapped

why: block (i,j) equals the inverted input iff input(i,j) is fg

reading: A grid of 2x2 cells separated by full lines; two cells of the same colour on one row or column are joined by filling the empty cells between them with that colour, the separator lines staying unchanged.

new_rows.name: gap
new_rows.datalog:
uneven(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), px(Y, X2, C2), C < C2.
sepc(C) :- px(Y, X, C), !uneven(Y).
gap(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y, X1, C), px(Y, X2, C), X1 < X, X < X2, C > 0, !sepc(C).
gap(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y1, X, C), px(Y2, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, C > 0, !sepc(C).

why: every 0 cell lying between two cells of one non-separator colour on its row or column takes that colour; no conflicts occur. Note the separator colour is the most common colour, so 0 is not the background here and the built-in 'between' row may not apply.

reading: A 3x3 arrangement of 3x3 panels split by lines of 5; the panel with the fewest coloured cells is a key, and each output panel is filled entirely with the key's cell at the same position (0 where the key is empty).

slots.key: the panel with fewest non-zero cells (4 vs 5)
slots.map: panel (i,j) of output filled with key(i,j)

why: every output panel is uniform with colour key(i,j)

reading: Each small cross (centre colour A, arms colour B) grows into a 5x5 star: the arms extend one more cell in each orthogonal direction in B, and the four diagonals get two cells each in A.

slots.colours: taken from each cross (vary per pair)

why: around every cross centre the 5x5 pattern (A diagonals, B orthogonals) is drawn; all else unchanged

reading: Connected shapes of 1 (blocks joined by thin corridors) each contain one seed cell of another colour; every interior cell of that connected shape (all 8 neighbours non-background) takes the seed colour.

slots.subject: each 8-connected non-background component containing a seed
slots.region: its cells whose 8 neighbours are all non-background

why: exactly the interior cells of seeded components change, to that component's seed colour; components without a seed and border cells of shapes are unchanged
